docs.title: Michael Beale
docs.text: I’m a software engineer and technical lead with 20+ years of experience across software security, research, and accessibility. At Intel Labs, I turned security, open-source, and responsible AI requirements into steps researchers could follow to release software and AI models. I’ve also modernized development tools and accessibility software, making them easier to test, maintain, and release.

docs.title: Selected accomplishments
docs.text:
• Redesigned Intel Labs’ software compliance workflow, reducing release timelines from weeks to hours.
  • Helped Intel publish its first public multimodal AI model by coordinating release requirements across Research, Legal, and executive stakeholders.
  • Reworked the Adaptive Contextual Aware Toolkit (ACAT), raising unit-test coverage from 0% to 85% and helping ship its first feature release in two years.

docs.title: Technical expertise
docs.text:
• Software engineering — C#, .NET, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, React, Node.js, GraphQL, and cross-platform desktop development.
  • Security and compliance — Secure development, threat modeling, vulnerability analysis, open-source licensing, software bills of materials, and responsible AI governance.
  • Build and release automation — CI/CD, GitHub Actions, cross-platform builds, automated testing, packaging, and artifact signing.
  • Research and accessibility — AI model release, dataset documentation, assistive technology, and accessible desktop and web interfaces.

docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I like figuring out how things work and making them easier for the next person. When I’m new to a problem, I read what I can, talk to people who know the details, and pull what I learn into a clear explanation. I especially enjoy helping someone through a process for the first time. I help them see what matters, give them a place to start, and stay with them until the job is done.

That’s what I enjoyed about building the Intel Labs Compliance Portal. Researchers had to piece together guidance from different places to release their software. I brought the policies, tools, and documentation together so teams could see what applied to their project and what to do next.

Outside work, I’ve followed my curiosity into LEGO robotics and, more recently, watercolor. Watercolor is well outside my comfort zone, which is part of why I’m proud I’ve stuck with it. It’s teaching me to slow down, be patient with myself, and make time for something I’m learning just because I want to.

docs.title: Intel Corporation
docs.text:
2011–Present

At Intel, I’ve worked across product security, research operations, and software engineering. A recurring part of my work has been turning security and release requirements into tools and guidance that engineering and research teams can use.

docs.title: Security Researcher and Product Security Expert
docs.text:
Research Operations, Intel Labs 2019–Present

  • Redesigned software compliance and release workflows, cutting release timelines from weeks to hours. Built the Intel Labs Compliance Portal to bring policies, tools, and documentation into one place.
  • Turned responsible AI requirements into guidance for researchers. Coordinated with Legal, Research, and executive stakeholders to help publish Intel’s first public multimodal AI model.
  • Led onboarding, live training, and hands-on support for Intel’s GitHub migration across hundreds of repositories.
  • Reworked the Adaptive Contextual Aware Toolkit (ACAT), raising unit-test coverage from 0% to 85% and enabling its first feature release in two years.
  • Served as acting technical lead during team turnover, mentoring engineers and delivering releases for disability-access initiatives.
  • Coordinated with Intel’s Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) to resolve a critical security vulnerability.

docs.title: PSEC Security Engineer
docs.text:
Software Security Engineering, PSD 2017–2019

  • Built a team wiki and engagement portal, and wrote secure development guidance covering compiler settings, coding standards, and defensive practices.
  • Supported security reviews for releases including Secure Device Onboarding and the Intel Crypto API Toolkit for SGX.
  • Coordinated Box Creek integration across teams in the U.S., Israel, and China, unifying CI pipelines and consolidating three repositories into one.
  • Led development of a reusable security testing framework for the Box Creek SDK, helping the team complete its Secure Development Lifecycle requirements.
  • Mentored a University of Michigan intern on fuzz testing, leading to a comparative evaluation framework and published results.

docs.title: Security Engineer
docs.text:
Cloud Services Group, Intel Services Division 2014–2016

  • Led an Intel SGX backend attestation code review that identified and reported more than 50 potential security defects for remediation.
  • Added digital signature validation and certificate pinning to the Software Asset Manager client.
  • Ported the Windows SDK to POSIX systems and contributed automated cross-platform acceptance tests.
  • Developed and taught an introductory security and cryptography course for Intel staff and interns.

docs.title: Security Engineer
docs.text:
Platform Enabling Services, Intel Services Division 2012–2014

  • Wrote TLS best practices adopted across Intel’s Software and Services Group and Intel SAFE.
  • Helped prototype a protocol for securely provisioning untrusted IoT gateways and connecting them to management systems.
  • Wrote API references and sample code documentation for the Intel Anti-Theft OS-Based Recovery SDK.

docs.title: Intel Contract Employee
docs.text:
Security and Privacy Research Lab, Intel Labs 2011–2012

  • Worked with the U.S. Air Force Academy’s Center of Innovation on secure group collaboration software using Intel SGX.
  • Defined security requirements, developed test plans, and ran security tests. Supported hands-on penetration testing with cadets and cybersecurity specialists.
  • Co-presented findings and live demos to Academy faculty and Department of Homeland Security representatives.
